chapter: New York: 52nd Street and Lester Young
title: Working with Lester Young: Birdland and the cat named Philharmonic
summary: Ramey worked with Ben Webster at the Onyx, then with Prez from 1948 at Birdland, remaining close.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, when do you get with Lester?
Now, Perez was across the street, and I was working with Ben. Perez was at the Spotlight, and I was with Ben.
And we -- Perez and I would get together. He was living in the Chesterfield, and I'd walk around there

with him and we'd go have breakfast and like that, just, you know, and he kept on trying to get me to come, but I was with Ben, you know. I said, well, now he got a little bass player out of Chicago. So -- and Roy Hanes and those guys. And so I went on with Lockjaw, went up to Minton's. Then I stayed at Minton's with Ben Webster when he came in.

And that folded up, and I told Perez, why I'll go with you. I went back, went with him in '48, and Gale sent us out on tours and things, and one time we went out, we had a jacket with us. Other times Perez went out and had his eight pieces, six or eight pieces, and then we played lots of clubs in Philadelphia.

And we had Joe Jones with us then, and we got Junior Mance. Then Perez, when I was with Jazz Philharmonic, at the when he came back, I had joined with Miles Davis. And that's when we -- that's when we opened in Birdland. Opposite and Pops said Lips Page, the opening band in Birdland, you know. And then Perez comes in, and Perez wants me to stay there with him. And he brings in John Lewis and Joe Jones, a quartet, so I stayed there with him.

And then Perez went back out with Norman Granz again and Joe and I and Milt Buckner stayed there with Gene Hammonds and Sonny Stitt team. And then Joe and I became the household members. Perez and I were like -- you know, whenever Perez was back home, I was -- unless I was already

committed, I'd go back with him and work, you know, and we renewed our old tight relationship, you know, I'd wait for him. When I was working with somebody else, and he got off early, I'd wait for him and take him home all the way, you know. At first he was living down at the Mark, at a hotel down on 43rd Street.
He always talks about his cat. He called her Philharmonic. And he said something to the cat one day, and the cat didn't like it and jumped out the window.
From the eighth floor. He insulted the cat. The cat jumped. So he said it hurt him so badly, but we were always tight.
